text: Every unit has an altitude level from 0 to 5. Ground units stay at 0; aircraft start at their type's cruise level.
tests: aircraft start at cruise altitude and ground units at 0
ground unit cannot spawn in the air

text: No aircraft may be placed or ordered above its type's ceiling.
tests: drone cannot spawn above its ceiling
altitude above the ceiling is rejected

text: An attacker must be at or below its release altitude to hit a ground target.
tests: an attacker descends to its release altitude
no hits land from above release altitude, hits land once it is down

text: Only fighters and missiles may attack aircraft, and must be within one level of the target.
tests: a fighter climbs or dives to its target's level and shoots it down in two hits

text: A contact at level 0 or 1 behind cover gives a weaker track; a low-signature aircraft gives a weaker track than a large one.
tests: a low contact behind cover is masked: weaker track and no lock; one level up it is seen
a stealth fighter gives a much weaker track than a bomber at the same place

text: Point defense stops a covered contact's hit, and suppresses a covered jammer, only when it has a lock on that contact.
tests: a defended missile is blocked and HQ takes no damage
a defended jammer's field is suppressed
defending a contact with no lock does not block it

text: An invalid command is refused with a reason and leaves the world unchanged.
tests: rejected commands leave the world unchanged
move off the map is rejected

text: The world is the same whether time advances in one call or many, and survives being saved and reloaded, including worlds saved by older versions.
tests: observed velocity persists across CLI calls
sequence score is the same for 4 ticks at once and 4 single ticks with reads in between
a world saved before altitude existed loads with aircraft at cruise level

text: A cease or move order ends a standing attack.
tests: a move order replaces a standing attack

text: Every order, spawn and reset is logged with who issued it, why, and the threat picture at that moment, whether accepted or refused.
tests: reset, accepted and refused orders are all logged; ticks are not
log entry records actor, reason, order and outcome
log entry carries the threat picture the decision was made on
refused orders are logged with the simulator's reason

text: No value supplied in a command can switch logging off or corrupt the log.
tests: a reason that looks like a flag is kept as text and cannot switch logging off
the log stays valid JSON with quotes and newlines in a reason

text: Orders given by the computer are logged under their own actor name with a reason.
tests: each opponent order is logged with actor 'opponent' and a reason
autopilot orders are logged as actor 'autopilot' with the behavior and a reason

text: The threat model reads only inputs blue can observe, and the simulator publishes the list so training code cannot drift from it.
tests: `inputs` lists the model's input names, history included
learned: observed vector matches the input list, all values in 0..1
the model sees altitude and descent

text: The C++ models give the same scores as their Python references on every held-out row.
Held-out accuracy and scripted-scenario results do not fall below their floors.
tests: learned AUC on air contacts at least 0.93
learned passes at least 12 scripted scenarios

text: Acting on the model's scores gives better outcomes than acting on the heuristics or at random.
tests: learned triage beats the heuristic that reads the target

text: With noise off, every contact is tracked exactly where it is, so earlier results are unchanged.
tests: sensing is perfect by default: every contact tracked exactly where it is
perfect picture tracks every contact with no error

text: A noisy run replays exactly from its seed.
tests: noisy sensing is reproducible: the same seed gives the same picture every tick
a different seed gives a different picture

text: The tracker keeps more contacts, loses fewer tracks and is closer to the truth than the best single detection.
tests: the tracker holds more contact-ticks and loses fewer tracks than the best single detection
the tracker's positions are closer to the truth than raw detections
under heavy noise the tracker loses fewer tracks

text: A contact with no track is invisible to the threat model and the planner.
tests: the planner's observation lists only contacts that have a track

text: The observation holds only what blue can measure. It never names a contact's target; it names a blue unit only once that unit has been hit.
tests: an observed contact carries only what blue can measure
the observation never names what a contact is attacking (nothing has been hit yet)
once a contact hits a blue unit, the observation says which unit it hit

text: A malformed message or an unknown message version is refused with an error, never a crash.
tests: a malformed message gets an error reply, not a crash
an unknown message version is refused

text: The node answers one plan per observation, in order, serves several connections at once, and accepts a new client after one disconnects.
tests: a TCP connection carries one plan per observation, in order
after a client disconnects the node accepts the next one
a second client is answered while the first stays connected
a client that has sent half a message does not hold up another

text: The edge node decides exactly as the planner inside the simulator does.
tests: the node agrees with the in-simulator planner on every tick
same mission value with the node in the loop

text: A reply that misses the tick budget is not used, and a dead link behaves exactly like no autonomy.
tests: no reply misses the tick budget on a direct link
with the link down, nothing from the node is used

text: The same interface is available as ROS 2 topics with typed messages: the simulator and the planner run as separate ROS 2 nodes, and the plan on the topic is exactly what the planner gives for that observation.
tests: an observation was published on the topic for every tick
a plan came back over the topic for every tick that was played
each plan matches the planner run directly on the same observation
the orders took effect: headquarters is defending in a later observation

text: Point defense covers the contact that can do the most damage next, not the one with the highest score regardless of timing, and never one it cannot lock.
tests: point defense covers the jet attacking now, not a missile still 8 ticks out
point defense switches to the missile once it can hit next tick
a contact with no lock is passed over for one that can be shot at

text: The planner gives no order to a unit that is already doing the right thing.
tests: no order is repeated when point defense is already on the right contact
already engaging the chosen target, it gets no new order
on station and orbiting, it gets no new order

text: The planner orders only blue units, and a fighter is never sent against a ground unit.
tests: the fighter never goes after a ground unit

text: The planner defends better than point defense alone and than either simpler fighter rule.
Hold fire: a fighter does not shoot at a contact the threat model has not labelled watch or hostile; it may follow it.
tests: hold fire: a contact below the watch line is shadowed, not shot at
a fighter that is merely close and has not fired is not shot at

text: Self-defense: a contact that has hit one of blue's aircraft may be shot at whatever its label, and a damaged fighter fights its hunter instead of running.
tests: self-defense: a contact that has hit our fighter is shot at even below the watch line
a damaged fighter does not turn and run from the contact hunting it: it fights
self-defense keeps the fighter alive more often

text: A damaged fighter starts no fight with an armed aircraft that has done nothing yet, and returns to headquarters if that is all there is; it keeps attacking aircraft that cannot shoot back and aircraft already seen hitting a blue unit.
tests: a damaged fighter leaves an armed aircraft that has done nothing alone and returns to headquarters
a damaged fighter still goes after a bomber, which cannot shoot back
a damaged fighter still goes after an armed aircraft already seen hitting a blue unit
a damaged fighter that stays in the battle shoots down more of red's aircraft

text: Red orders only red units, and its coordinated strike arrives together and low.
tests: red opponent never orders blue units
under the coordinated doctrine at least three attackers land their first hit within three ticks of each other
jets and drones come in at level 1

text: The coordinated doctrine was harder on the planner than the original script before the planner was taught to answer it, and the planner still beats no defense against it.
tests: the coordinated doctrine hurt the planner more than the original script before it was taught
the planner still beats no defense against the coordinated doctrine

text: Autopilot is offered for whichever side the player commands. It orders only that side, and the computer keeps flying the other.
tests: autopilot can be switched on when commanding red
autopilot can be switched on when commanding blue
red autopilot orders red units, and only red units
blue autopilot orders blue units, and only blue units
with red on autopilot the computer still flies blue against it

text: With autopilot off a side does nothing until the player orders it, a player can order only their own side, and a game stops at tick 20.
tests: with autopilot off, red does nothing until the player orders it
a red player still cannot order blue's units
a red game played by hand runs to tick 20 and then refuses to go on

text: Every visitor has a separate world, game, clock and autopilot switches. Visitors doing the same thing at the same time get exactly the same result, and parallel requests in one session are applied one after another.
tests: visitors doing the same thing at the same time end with exactly the same result
sandbox switches changed by some visitors did not change anyone else's
a client that sends no session id is untouched by all of them
eight ticks sent at once in one session all count, exactly once each

text: The console opens in a Basic view for a first-time visitor: units are named in words, a battle can be watched or played in one or two taps, and none of the technical console shows. An Advanced view holds the full console on the same battle. The visitor's choice is remembered, and a link can ask for either with ?level=.
tests: browser: a first visit on a phone opens in Basic, with three ways in and none of the console
browser: Watch a battle hands both sides to the computer and shows the scoreboard
browser: Send fighter reaches the simulator as an order, and is confirmed in a sentence
browser: Advanced shows the whole console on the same battle and hides Basic
browser: the level is remembered across a reload
a link can ask for either level, and wins over the saved choice

text: Basic tells a battle in plain words. Every hit, block and failed lock the simulator reports gets one sentence and one flag on the map, a round where nothing lands still says what each side is doing, and no unit id or simulator term appears anywhere in it.
tests: in a real battle the computer plays, every hit, block and failed lock the simulator reports gets a sentence
the same holds when a visitor attacks as red and when one leaves blue undefended
no round in any of them left the visitor with nothing to read
no sentence the Basic view said in any of this contains a unit id or a simulator term
browser: a round where something landed is told in as many sentences, flagged in as many places, in plain words
browser: the map names every unit in a word, and nothing on the page is a unit id or a simulator term

text: What Basic says is true of the simulator. Every unit type has a name, each aircraft's description matches its numbers in the C++ tables, an attack the simulator would refuse is not offered, the strength shown is the sum the server scores a game with, and a visitor is only told they beat the computer when they did.
tests: every unit type the simulator has gets a plain name and a description
what Basic says about each aircraft is true of the simulator's numbers
which aircraft may attack aircraft is the simulator's own table
a bomber or a drone cannot be sent at an aircraft, and anything can be sent at the ground
blue's strength, averaged over a real battle, is the score the server reports
a watched battle's score is offered as the one to beat, and beating it is only claimed when it happened

text: One Dockerfile builds the console, the planner and the test tools. The planner image holds a single statically linked file and nothing else.
tests: the console, planner and tools images build
the planner image holds one file, the planner, and it is under 5 MB
the simulator's and the planner's own test suites pass inside the tools image

text: Containers run as a non-root user with no Linux capabilities on a read-only filesystem; the console can write only to its data volume, and saved worlds outlive the container.
tests: each container runs as a non-root user with no capabilities, on a read-only filesystem
the console can write to its data volume and nowhere else in its image
worlds survive the console container being replaced

text: With the simulator in one container and the planner in another, held to half a CPU core and 32 MB, software-in-the-loop still passes: same orders as the in-simulator planner and no reply over the tick budget.
tests: software-in-the-loop passes with the simulator and the planner in separate containers
the planner container is held to half a CPU core and 32 MB of memory
the planner answers on its published port, which is open to this machine only

text: A container can tell whether it is healthy and stops at once when asked: the planner checks itself with --ping, and both programs exit with status 0 on a stop request.
tests: the console and the planner start and report healthy
asked to stop, both containers exit within three seconds with status 0
--ping reports a live node, even while other clients are connected
asked to terminate, the node stops at once with status 0
asked to terminate, the server stops at once with status 0

text: The ROS 2 bridge runs from an image with no ROS installed on the host: the demo plays its ticks and stops, and the bridge check passes inside the image.
tests: the ROS 2 demo plays its ticks over the topics and then stops by itself
the bridge check passes inside the ROS 2 image

text: The learned policy is given the same observation message as the planner and nothing else, and its reward is the mission value every evaluation reports.
tests: observe reports blue's mission value beside the observation, not inside it
the reward adds up to the mission value the evaluations report
every picture has the declared number of inputs

text: Hold fire is enforced on the learned policy as a mask on its choices: a shot at a contact below the watch line is never offered unless that contact has hit one of blue's aircraft, and the orders it gives are checked against the rule from outside.
tests: hold fire: the fighter is not offered a contact scored below the watch line
self-defense: a contact that has hit one of blue's aircraft is offered whatever its score
in every picture from real games, the masks follow the same rules
the shipped policy only ever picks a choice the rules offer
no order to shoot breaks the hold-fire rule

text: Training is reproducible and runs on the simulator itself: the served simulator gives the same game as the command line, and the same seeds and choices give the same games.
tests: a served rollout matches the command line, apart from rounding in the last digits
served and command-line rollouts give the same orders and the same events
the same seeds and the same choices give the same games, tick for tick

text: The shipped policy is worth having: it beats no defense on games it never trained on and covers at least half the distance to the planner.
tests: the learned policy beats no defense on the scripted rollouts
the learned policy beats no defense against red's doctrine
the learned policy covers at least half the distance from no defense to the planner
